title: Correlation values, each with the n it was computed on

rule.sourcing: both sides of every pair must come from a sourced, recorded file; an unsourced pair is published as NOT SOURCED even if it would compute
rule.intervals: 2000 bootstrap resamples per value, 2000 permutation draws for the p-value, fixed seed 20261114 so the page is reproducible

families.title: Within-game outcome correlations
families.why_it_matters: these are the joints a parlay actually carries

rows.name: Home margin vs game total
rows.note: The correlation a same-game side+total parlay is exposed to. A positive value means games that go over also tend to be won by more. NFL margin and total are close to independent, and this row is how close.

rows.name: Home margin vs market spread
rows.note: A validity check on the upstream: the market spread must correlate strongly with the actual margin or the price store's sign convention is wrong. The sign is negative because both columns use the home-team convention (negative = home favoured): a market of -7 goes with a positive home margin.

rows.name: Game total vs market total
rows.note: Same validity check for the total. r = 0.32 is low in absolute terms because a book's total is a fair price, not a forecast of the realised score: the residual is the variance the market cannot remove, and that residual is the only thing a total model can win.

families.title: Model vs market agreement
families.why_it_matters: validity, not edge: a model that does not move with the market is not measuring the same thing

rows.name: Originated side vs market side
rows.note: Agreement with the market is not skill -- it is the minimum bar a model has to clear before its disagreements can mean anything.

rows.name: Originated total vs market total
rows.note: Agreement with the market is not skill -- it is the minimum bar a model has to clear before its disagreements can mean anything.

rows.name: Originated home win probability vs market-implied
rows.note: The market probability still contains the vig, so the market column is systematically above 0.5 for favourites; the correlation is still meaningful.

families.title: Required but not computable from sourced numbers
families.why_it_matters: published as gaps rather than estimated

rows.name: Player-prop leg correlation (receptions vs receiving yards, same player)
rows.why: No prop price and no prop outcome is reachable from this environment. The nflverse release assets that carry player stats are hosted on a domain this sandbox cannot reach (recorded in data/lab/upstream/_pin.json).
rows.what_would_close_it: A licensed prop feed, or a league-published gamebook, for two seasons, so the same-player legs can be paired.

rows.name: Injury count vs margin (the owner's availability thesis)
rows.why: The injury report on this snapshot covers one week; a per-game injury count for two seasons is the minimum for this pair, and the league report is not reachable in bulk from this sandbox.
rows.what_would_close_it: Weekly injury reports archived for 2+ seasons (Q-L4).

rows.name: Cross-strategy profit correlation
rows.why: Requires a settled ticket list per strategy; the leaderboard's strategies are on paper and have no settled live tickets.
rows.what_would_close_it: Two seasons of paper tickets logged per strategy.

families.title: Strategy overlap (from executed picks)
families.why_it_matters: two strategies on the same games are one strategy dressed as two
